title: Justified still stumble daily (James, Eccl, Prov, 1 John)
source_text: XX. Unde fit ut qui sunt per Christi gratiam justificati & sanctificati, nihilominus in varia peccata ex infirmitate quotidie incurrant, juxta illud Jacobi, In multis offendimus omnes, Jac. 3. Et Salomonis in Ecclesiastae, Non est homo justus in terra, qui faciat bonum, & non peccet. Eccl. 7. Item in Proverbiis, Quis potest dicere, Mundum est cor meum, purus sum a peccato? Prov. 20. Quo respiciens Joannes pronunciat, Quod si dixerimus nos peccatum non habere, ipsi nos seducimus, & veritas in nobis non est. 1 Joan. 1.
pass_a_gloss: Hence it happens that those who are justified and sanctified by Christ's grace nevertheless daily fall into various sins from infirmity, according to that of James: In many things we all offend (James 3). And of Solomon in Ecclesiastes: There is no just man on earth who does good and does not sin (Ecclesiastes 7). Likewise in Proverbs: Who can say, My heart is clean, I am pure from sin? (Proverbs 20). Looking to which John pronounces: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us (1 John 1).
pass_b_english: Even the justified stumble daily from weakness (James 3; Ecclesiastes 7; Proverbs 20).

lemmas.gloss: in many things we all offend
